notes: Merthyr Tydfil has no selective or additional licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: three or more storeys, five or more occupiers, two or more households. Separately, all landlords in Wales must register with Rent Smart Wales, a different national scheme.
research: NEGATIVE, SOURCED. The council's HMO Licence page describes ONLY mandatory licensing, in the Welsh three-storey form: 'The Housing Act 2004 places a duty on local authorities in Wales to licence houses in multiple occupation (HMOs). This is known as mandatory licensing... The scheme only applies to houses in multiple occupation that meet the following criteria: The houses in multiple occupation or any part of it comprises three storeys or more; and It is occupied by five or more persons; and It is occupied by person living in two or more single households, with a sharing of facilities.' This matches WSI 2006/1712 (W.174). No designation, area, dates or discretionary scheme is named anywhere. RAW-HTML GREP of both HMO pages returned ZERO hits for 'selectiv', 'additional licen' and 'dewisol'; the raw HTML was grepped, not rendered text, so nothing hidden in JSON or JS payloads was missed. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is HTTP 404, but robots.txt discloses the bare-path Umbraco sitemap. That returned 1,504 URLs, grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol', 'amlfedd', 'hmo' and 'multiple-occup': the ONLY two housing-licensing URLs on the entire site are the resident and business HMO pages. There is no selective or additional licensing page in either language. The 56 'licen' URLs are taxi, alcohol and entertainment, sex establishment, scrap metal and child performance licensing. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) the s.254 and s.257 DEFINITION, recited on the resident HMO page as 'Defined under sections 254 and 257 of the Housing Act 2004, an HMO can be a building or part of a building if it is: occupied by persons who form more than one household, and where those persons share (or lack) one or more basic amenities'. That defines an HMO, NOT a licensing threshold. (2) RENT SMART WALES, the national regime under the Housing (Wales) Act 2014 applying to every landlord in Wales. Not a Part 2 s.56 or Part 3 designation and NOT recorded as a scheme. (3) The council's inspection database ('The Section holds a database of these premises which are inspected on a risk based programme') is a risk-based inspection programme, not a designation. LIMITATIONS: the council's own site search was not relied on. The negative rests on the explicit mandatory-only wording, the raw-HTML greps and the complete 1,504-URL sitemap sweep. WebSearch was unavailable, so all evidence is direct HTTP fetch from merthyr.gov.uk only. The 'Information for Applicant booklet' PDF was not retrieved, so no fee figure is quoted; this does not affect the finding, because a discretionary scheme would have to be designated and published, and no designation exists anywhere on the site.

notes: Monmouthshire has no selective or additional licensing. The council states only mandatory HMO licensing applies: three or more storeys, five or more occupiers, two or more households. Separately, all Welsh landlords must register with Rent Smart Wales, a separate scheme.
research: NEGATIVE, TWO INDEPENDENT PRIMARY SOURCES, ONE AN EXPRESS DOUBLE DISCLAIMER. (1) The council's Housing Standards page (JSON-LD dateModified 2026-03-05, so current) states verbatim in the raw HTML: 'In Monmouthshire there is only one type of licensing - Mandatory Licensing'. Threshold quoted in the Welsh three-storey form. The Welsh page says the same: 'Yn Sir Fynwy nid oes ond un math o drwyddedu mewn grym, sef Trwyddedu Gorfodol.' (2) DECISIVE: the HMO licensing policy the council itself links to, section 20 headed 'Discretionary HMO licensing', expressly disclaims BOTH powers: 'We do not intend to apply for additional discretionary powers to extend the licensing of all HMOs in a specific area... Such powers are not necessary in Monmouthshire at present as there are no areas where several HMOs are linked to anti social behaviour. Similarly we do not intend to apply for new powers to introduce selective licensing for all private sector housing (including non HMOs) in designated areas... These additional powers are not necessary as there are no areas of low housing demand in the County and no problems with anti social behaviour associated with particular types or areas of housing at present.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: section 15 of the same policy lists only two lines, 'HMO Licence first time application - £500' and 'HMO Licence renewal application - £450'. A flat mandatory-only pair with no per-property fee, no small-HMO fee and no separate application route. SITEMAP SWEEP: all seven page and post sitemaps pulled (5,421 URLs) and grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol', 'hmo', 'multiple-occup' and 'amlfedd'. Zero licensing-scheme pages. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES: the Landlord Hub says 'Any Landlord issuing a domestic occupation contract for a property in Wales must be registered with Rent Smart Wales to comply with the law' and that self-managing landlords 'must also have a licence'. That is the Housing (Wales) Act 2014 NATIONAL regime and is the dominant Welsh false positive, being the reason a landlord can correctly be told they 'need a licence' anywhere in Wales while no local designation exists. (2) WELSH-LANGUAGE HOMONYMS: every sitemap hit for 'ychwanegol' is 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol' (additional LEARNING needs) or 'cyllid ychwanegol' (additional funding); every 'dewisol' hit is 'taliadau tai dewisol' (DISCRETIONARY housing payments) or 'addysg ddewisol yn y cartref' (elective home education). There is also an English decoy, a news item about 'selective mowing' to promote meadow management. (3) The s.254 DEFINITION on the HMO page. (4) A GOV.UK LINK to national guidance. (5) MONMOUTHSHIRE LETTING SERVICE, a council lettings and leasing incentive scheme whose page is titled 'Landlord registration and licencing'; its 'licencing' is Rent Smart Wales, and a voluntary lettings scheme is not a designation. LIMITATIONS: Monmouthshire's WordPress site search is client-side only; the control query and the nonsense negative control both return an identical ~12,928-byte shell with no server-rendered results, so a nil result from it proves NOTHING and none was relied on. Its ModernGov document search is also broken: the controls 'budget' and 'housing' both return 'No results found for your query' at every DocType, so its nil results carry no weight either. Neither failure blocks the conclusion, because the council's own current page and its own linked policy state the position explicitly and the sitemap sweep is comprehensive.

schemes.areaDescription: The White City area of Aberavon, Port Talbot, as shown on the plan attached to the Cabinet Board report

notes: No licensing scheme runs here now. A selective licensing scheme covered the White City area of Aberavon from May 2009 to May 2014 and was not renewed. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies today: three or more storeys and five or more occupiers.
research: A GENUINE PART 3 SELECTIVE DESIGNATION EXISTED HERE AND HAS EXPIRED. NO s.56 SCHEME EVER. NOTHING LIVE TODAY. THIS FINDING DISPROVES THE WORKING ASSUMPTION THAT NO PART 3 DESIGNATION HAS EVER BEEN MADE IN WALES. DESIGNATION MADE, VERIFIED VERBATIM from the primary minutes: Social Care, Health and Housing Cabinet Board, 30 January 2009, item 6, 'PROPOSED SELECTIVE LICENSING SCHEME IN THE AREA'. The minutes were downloaded and text-extracted directly. They record a DECISION, not merely a proposal: 'That, with effect from the 5th May, 2009 the area of Aberavon shown on the plan attached to the circulated report, be designated as subject to selective licensing pursuant to Section 80(1) of the Housing Act 2004; That the designation, as set out in Paragraph 1 above, cease to have effect on the 4th May, 2014 unless otherwise revoked in the proper manner under Section 88(4) of the Housing Act 2004; That the Principal Officer Environmental Health publish Notice of the making of the above designation, in accordance with the statutory requirements; That the Principal Officer Environmental Health be authorised to manage a Licensing Scheme for houses in the said area pursuant to this designation... That the above designation be kept under review... under Section 84 of the Housing Act 2004'. s.80(1) is the Part 3 designation power and s.88(4) the duration provision, so the statutory basis is unambiguous. Prior consultation was authorised on 6 Nov 2007. IT OPERATED: the Environmental Health enforcement policies of 17/03/2011, 04/04/2013 and 13/03/2014 each state 'The Environmental Health Service operates a selective licensing scheme within the county borough to address problems associated with high numbers of private rented properties and increased levels of antisocial behaviour. Landlords must obtain a license.' A March 2014 Renewal Area report records 'Selective Licensing for landlords introduced into the White City area of Aberavon to tackle high levels of ASB, high level of private rented properties (over 40%) and high levels of vacant properties.' IT LAPSED AND WAS NOT RENEWED: the June 2018 Enforcement Policy reproduces the SAME boilerplate paragraph with the selective licensing sentence DELETED, leaving only: 'The service also operates a Mandatory Licensing Scheme to regulate high risk houses in multiple occupation (HMOs), of 3 or more storeys occupied by 5 or more people not of the same family. Further powers are available should the authority decide to utilise them for the control of 2 storey HMOs.' A paged sweep of the ModernGov archive for the exact phrases 'White City' and 'selective licensing' returns NOTHING dated after 13/03/2014. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, DECISIVE FOR THE POSITION TODAY: the environmental health fees page has a table headed 'Housing in multiple occupation licensing schemes' / 'Statutory Fees' containing exactly ONE licence fee, 'Licence of 3 Storey + £718.97', plus 'HMO Consultation Fee £77.48'. There is NO selective, NO additional, NO flat per-property and NO two-storey HMO fee. A live self-financing scheme could not exist without one. SITE SWEEP: the HTML sitemap (1,557 links) contains exactly one HMO item. Zero pages matching 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol' or 'amlfedd'. The consultations page lists no licensing consultation, so there is nothing to record as proposed. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES. (2) STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL: 'Further powers are available should the authority decide to utilise them for the control of 2 storey HMOs' describes the s.56 power as expressly UNEXERCISED, and is the single most likely source of a false positive here. (3) THE CARAVAN-SITE FEE LADDER on the same fees page ('Number of units: 5-10 £355.56, 11-20 £414.81') is Caravan Sites and Control of Development Act licensing, checked in context so it was not mistaken for a s.56 cost-recovery ladder. (4) ModernGov OR-matching noise. WARDS: deliberately null. The designation is defined by a named area shown on a plan, inside Aberavon, so coverage is 'areas' and NO WARD LIST HAS BEEN SYNTHESISED. The designation also predates the major Welsh ward boundary changes at the May 2022 elections, so any ward name carried over would very likely be stale. LIMITATIONS: NPT's website search is Google Custom Search rendered client-side and its nils prove nothing; the 1,557-link HTML sitemap was used instead. By contrast NPT's ModernGov search PASSED both controls, so its post-2014 silence IS evidence. No published fee was found for the 2009-2014 scheme, so feeApprox is null rather than guessed.

schemes.areaDescription: All wards of the City of Newport. Covers every HMO outside mandatory licensing that houses three or more people in more than two households.
schemes.feeApprox: £1,439.78 for a 3-5 person HMO; 6+ adds £78.70 per unit to a maximum of £1,991.84

schemes.areaDescription: Predecessor scheme, the Newport City Council Houses in Multiple Occupation Licensing Scheme 2019. Its expiry left a gap with no additional licensing in force until 13 February 2025.

notes: Newport runs an additional HMO licensing scheme across every ward of the city, so almost all HMOs need a council licence, not just larger ones. It runs from 13 February 2025 to 12 February 2030. Fees start at £1,439.78 for a three to five person HMO.
research: ACTIVE s.56 ADDITIONAL LICENSING, CITY-WIDE. THE SEALED DESIGNATION WAS VERIFIED VERBATIM by downloading and extracting the council's own PDF, linked from its additional licensing page. It reads: 'NEWPORT CITY COUNCIL HOUSES IN MULTIPLE OCCUPATION LICENSING SCHEME 2024. Newport City Council of the Civic Centre Newport NP20 4UR in exercise of their powers under Section 56 of the Housing Act 2004 hereby make the following Scheme. CITATION, COMMENCEMENT AND REVOCATION 1.1 This scheme may be cited as the Newport City Council Houses in Multiple Occupation Licensing Scheme 2024 and is made pursuant to Section 56 of the Housing Act 2004 and the Housing Act 2004 (Additional HMO Licensing) (Wales) General Approval 2007. 1.2 This scheme shall come into force on the 13th February 2025 and shall cease to have effect on the 12th February 2030 (unless revoked beforehand). 1.3 This Scheme replaces the Newport City Council Houses in Multiple Occupation Licensing Scheme 2019 which expired on the 30th of June 2024.' AREA, clause 3: 'This Scheme shall apply to all wards of the City of Newport.' APPLICATION, clause 4: 'This Scheme shall apply to all HMOs (other than those which fall within the mandatory licensing regime) which house three or more persons forming more than two single households.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED DECISIVELY: the council's HMO licensing application advice document, fee schedule footer-dated '1st April 26', sets out two columns, 'Smaller HMOs (3-5 units/households)' and 'Larger HMOs (6+ units/households)': 'New/Initial application £1,439.78 | £78.70 extra per unit/household (maximum £1,991.84); Renewal application before expiration £1,073.87; Renewal application after expiration £1,358.29; Application following revocation of previous licence £1,073.87. Licence Variations: Property inspection required £122.69. Cancellation Charge £35.08.' THE LADDER STARTS AT THREE UNITS, NOT FIVE. A mandatory-only authority's ladder starts at five occupiers, so a dedicated cost-recovery band for sub-mandatory 3-5 person HMOs is exactly the tell of a genuine s.56 scheme, and it corroborates clause 4. THE GAP IS REAL AND MATTERS: the 2019 scheme expired 30 June 2024 and the 2024 scheme did not commence until 13 February 2025, so for that period no additional licensing was in force in Newport. Any historic liability question falling in that window must not be answered from the current designation. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING: the full sitemap was swept (an index of two pages, 3,108 URLs) and grepped for 'selectiv' and 'dewisol'. ZERO hits in either language. The only HMO URLs are the eight pages under the HMO branch. WARDS: the designation says 'all wards of the City of Newport', so coverage is borough-wide with wards null. This is the safe encoding: it avoids enumerating ward names, so the major Welsh ward boundary changes at the May 2022 elections cannot break matching. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES, which applies to every Newport landlord regardless; the s.56 finding rests solely on the sealed designation and the fee schedule. (2) PLANNING: 'Under the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987, shared houses with 3 or more occupiers need planning consent' is planning control, never licensing. (3) The s.254 DEFINITION in clause 2. (4) CIVIL-PENALTY BOILERPLATE about s.72(1), which appears regardless of any designation. THE PREDECESSOR RECORD: the 2019 scheme is recorded as expired because the 2024 designation names it and its expiry date explicitly. The 2019 designation itself was NOT retrieved, so its start date is null and its stated area is not independently verified; it is encoded as borough-wide only because it is the direct predecessor the 2024 city-wide scheme 'replaces', and that inference is flagged here rather than presented as verified fact. Only the 30 June 2024 expiry is directly quoted from a primary source.

notes: Pembrokeshire has no selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: three or more storeys and five or more occupiers. The council confirmed in 2024 it had no plans to introduce either. Rent Smart Wales registration is a separate national requirement.
research: NEGATIVE, SOURCED, WITH AN EXPRESS COUNCIL STATEMENT. (1) The council's HMO page (footer revised 03/12/2025) sets out only mandatory licensing: 'Do all houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) have to be licensed? No... The Housing Act 2004 says that certain types of larger HMOs must be licensed - this is Mandatory Licensing. This covers HMOs that are: Three or more storeys high and, Are occupied by 5 or more persons who do not form a single household.' This retains the Welsh three-storey test. A raw-HTML grep returns ZERO hits for 'selectiv', 'additional licen', 'dewisol' and 'ychwanegol', and its meta keywords and meta description are BOTH EMPTY; this was checked specifically for the Wigan-style trap where 'Selective licensing' is smuggled into meta keywords without appearing in the body. It is not present. (2) DECISIVE: the council's own FOI disclosure log (received 24/01/2024, response from Directorate: Public Protection, response date 16/02/2024). Question 5 asked 'What schemes are you looking to introduce, i.e. selective/ additional?' The council answered: 'There are no currently no plans to introduce any additional HMO or selective licensing schemes.' (the council's own typo, reproduced verbatim). An express negative from the authority itself, on the exact question. (3) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the housing fees and charges page (revised 07/04/2026) contains, across 2025-26 and 2026-27, exactly ONE housing line: 'ECO 4 Flex Declarations £175.00'. There is no additional or selective licensing fee anywhere. (4) REGISTER TEST: the public register of licensed HMOs lists nine properties (Blackpool Farm Narberth 3 storeys/12 occupants, Melbourne House Pembroke 3/19, 23 Hill Street Haverfordwest 3/20, Nelson Guest House 3/15, 14 Gloucester Terrace 3/6, 35 London Road Pembroke Dock 3/10, Penydre Saundersfoot 3/6, Manor House Lydstep 3/8, 9 Pembroke Street Pembroke Dock 3/16). EVERY ONE is three storeys with five or more occupants, purely the mandatory threshold. An additional scheme would necessarily place sub-mandatory HMOs on the register; not one appears. (5) SITEMAP SWEEP: 2,296 URLs. The only private-housing pages are the seven under the enforcement branch. (6) The closed-consultations list contains only a Licensing Act 2003 alcohol policy consultation, so there is nothing to record as proposed. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES, for which Pembrokeshire hosts a dedicated page. (2) HOLIDAY-LET AND SECOND-HOME MEASURES: Pembrokeshire's council tax premiums and Article 4 directions around Tenby and Saundersfoot are taxation and planning instruments respectively, NEVER licensing; checked specifically, and no Part 3 designation has ever been consulted on. (3) The s.254 DEFINITION ('Occupied by 3 or more people, forming 2 or more households'). (4) The SEO META-KEYWORD TRAP, explicitly checked and absent. (5) Base64 and JS-hidden content, checked; the only long base64 blobs are ASP.NET viewstate. LIMITATIONS: Pembrokeshire's own site search FAILED the control test and CANNOT support a nil finding. It is a Google Custom Search rendered client-side: 'selective licensing' (28,318 bytes), 'additional licensing' (28,319), 'houses in multiple occupation' (28,328), the Welsh 'trwyddedu dewisol' (28,316) and the nonsense NEGATIVE CONTROL (28,318) all returned near-identical HTML differing only in the CSRF token. The ModernGov portal redirects its search to the same broken engine, so committee full-text search was unavailable and no committee-record negative is claimed. The negative rests on the FOI answer, the fee schedule, the register composition and the sitemap sweep.

notes: Powys has no selective or additional licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, with fees from £750. Separately, every landlord in Wales must register with Rent Smart Wales, which is a national scheme and not council licensing.
research: NEGATIVE, SOURCED. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST IS DECISIVE: the entire housing licence fee page reads 'Houses in Multiple Occupation Fees. Mandatory HMO Licence Fees: The Basic licence fee is £750 for up to 5 rooms and must be paid in full with the application. There will be an additional charge for 6 - 10 rooms of £25 per room, 11 or more rooms will attract an additional charge of £40 per room.' A MANDATORY-ONLY ladder with a per-room surcharge, no flat per-property fee, no small-HMO fee and no separate application route. The HMO licensing page says only 'Landlords that own certain types of HMO have to apply for a licence' and never names a designation, area or dates. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED, STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL: the Enforcement and Complaints page states 'The Housing Act 2004 also allows for HMOs to be inspected and if necessary be licenced under either mandatory or additional HMO Licensing Schemes with associated fees... Local Authorities also have discretion to introduce additional licensing of other HMOs falling outside the scope of mandatory licensing... Note: it is an offence to operate a Mandatory HMO or a HMO covered by an Additional HMO Licensing Scheme without a licence.' This describes the POWER and the GENERIC OFFENCE, never its exercise in Powys. Read alone it would produce a false positive, and it is the single most dangerous passage on the site. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED, RENT SMART WALES: Powys has two RSW pages and the enforcement page says 'From October 2015, the Welsh Government introduced a new Welsh scheme requiring landlords of all rented property, regardless of size, to hold a licence and pay a fee.' That is the Housing (Wales) Act 2014 national regime, and is precisely why a Powys landlord can correctly be told they need 'a licence' while no local designation exists. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED: the '£25/£40 additional charge per room', a surcharge on a MANDATORY licence. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED: the s.254 DEFINITION ('let to 3 or more tenants who form 2 or more households'). TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED: 'Additional Learning Needs' and 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol' pages, which dominate the sitemap on the token 'additional' and 'ychwanegol'. EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE: (a) the full sitemap (3,779 URLs) grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol' and 'licen' contains no selective or additional licensing page; (b) THE SITE SEARCH PASSED BOTH CONTROLS, the positive control 'multiple occupation' returning 126 results including both HMO pages, and the nonsense NEGATIVE CONTROL returning zero results with no results block; against that working engine 'selective licensing' and 'additional licensing' returned only OR-matched generic licensing pages with no scheme page, so this nil result is genuine evidence; (c) the ModernGov committee document search ALSO PASSED its negative control, and 'selective licensing' returned just two irrelevant results (Taxi Licensing Sub-Committee minutes 30/01/2025; Local Housing Strategy 2016-2020, Cabinet 22/03/2016), while 'additional licensing scheme' returned only Building Control charges and planning applications. No designation exists in the committee record. Other landlord pages checked and clear. The Welsh mandatory threshold is confirmed in the council's own words: 'a three-storey building with five or more persons in occupation who share facilities'. LIMITATIONS: no 403s or bot blocks were encountered; Powys serves 302 redirects to a cookie-consent URL but full content returns with -L --compressed.

schemes.areaDescription: All electoral wards in Rhondda Cynon Taf. Covers every HMO except those exempt and those already caught by mandatory licensing.
Predecessor scheme, the Rhondda Cynon Taf Additional Licensing (Houses in Multiple Occupation) Scheme 2009, revoked on 31 March 2024 and replaced the next day with no gap in cover.

notes: Rhondda Cynon Taf runs an additional HMO licensing scheme covering every electoral ward, so almost all HMOs need a council licence, not just larger ones. It runs from 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2029. There is no selective licensing.
research: ACTIVE s.56 ADDITIONAL LICENSING, BOROUGH-WIDE. THE PUBLIC NOTICE WAS VERIFIED VERBATIM by fetching the page with browser headers and extracting the body text: 'Notice is hereby given that on the 21st December 2023 Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough Council has confirmed the designation of an additional licensing scheme in respect of Houses in Multiple Occupation covering all electoral wards in Rhondda Cynon Taf... The confirmation of the designation is in accordance with Section 56 - 60 of The Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006. The Scheme to which the designation applies has General Approval of the Welsh Assembly Government under the Housing Act 2004 (Additional HMO Licensing Wales) General Approval 2007... The Scheme applies to all Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) within the area described above, except those exempted by the relevant sections of the Act and those licensable under the Orders and Regulations made pursuant to Section 55 (2)(a) of the Housing Act 2004 (Mandatory Licensing). The Scheme will be effective from 1st April 2024 and unless revoked beforehand or extended will cease to have effect on 31st March 2029. The Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough Council Additional Licensing (Houses in Multiple Occupation) Scheme 2009 shall be revoked on the 31st March 2024. All licences issued under this scheme that remain in force at 31st March 2024 shall transfer to the new scheme and remain valid until they expire or are otherwise revoked by the Council or are surrendered.' IMPORTANT DOCUMENT DEFECT, FLAGGED: the notice mislabels the scheme as the 'Scheme 2014'. That is plainly a stale copy-paste in the council's own text; the designation was confirmed on 21 December 2023, runs 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2029, and revokes a 'Scheme 2009'. The OPERATIVE DATES are unambiguous and are what has been recorded; the citation name must not be relied on and must not be read as evidence of a 2014 scheme. COVERAGE: the notice says 'covering all electoral wards in Rhondda Cynon Taf', so coverage is borough-wide with wards NULL. This is the safe encoding: it avoids enumerating ward names entirely, so the major Welsh ward boundary changes at the May 2022 elections cannot break matching in either direction. CONTINUITY: the predecessor 2009 scheme was revoked on 31 March 2024 and the new scheme took effect on 1 April 2024, so there was NO GAP in cover, and existing licences were expressly transferred. The 2009 scheme is recorded as expired with end 2024-03-31 as quoted; its start date is not stated in this notice and the 2009 designation itself was not retrieved, so start is null and its coverage is inferred from it being the direct predecessor rather than independently verified. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING, EVIDENCED: the full RCT sitemap was swept (7,951 URLs, both EN and CY trees) and grepped for 'selectiv' and 'dewisol'. ZERO hits in either language. A raw-HTML grep of the public notice page itself also returns zero 'selectiv'. The only additional-licensing URLs on the entire site are the EN and CY versions of this one public notice. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES, for which RCT has a dedicated page; NOT recorded as a scheme, and the finding rests solely on the confirmed designation notice. (2) VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION: RCT operates a 'Property Accreditation Scheme'. (3) ENFORCEMENT PRESS RELEASES ('Pontypridd HMO Landlord Fined OVER 1500', Jan 2025; 'Landlord FINED for Illegally Operating HMO', Feb 2025) are prosecutions, not designations; they corroborate active enforcement but are not the basis of the finding. (4) The s.254 definition and s.72(1) unlimited-fine boilerplate. LIMITATIONS AND WHAT COULD NOT BE REACHED: no fee figure could be retrieved. The HMO landing page returns HTTP 200 with a ZERO-BYTE body through the council's Varnish cache, both gzip and identity encoding; guessed sub-page URLs return 404 from outside and do not appear in the sitemap. feeApprox is therefore left NULL rather than guessed. This does not affect the licensing determination, which rests on the confirmed statutory designation quoted verbatim above.

schemes.areaDescription: All HMOs of any size in the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas wards, including poorly converted blocks of flats. University-owned and managed student accommodation is exempt.

notes: Swansea runs additional HMO licensing in the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas wards, where every HMO needs a licence whatever its size. It runs 14 February 2026 to 14 February 2031, with fees from £1,096. Elsewhere only mandatory HMO licensing applies.
research: ACTIVE s.56 ADDITIONAL LICENSING, FRESHLY RE-DESIGNATED. The designation and the fee schedule were verified verbatim. The statutory public notice (last modified 16 February 2026) reads: 'Notice is hereby given that the City and County of Swansea has confirmed the designation of an additional licensing scheme in respect of houses in multiple occupation in the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas Electoral Wards. This scheme will be known as The City and County of Swansea's Additional HMO Licensing Scheme 2025. The confirmation of the designation is in accordance with Section 56 - 60 of The Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006. The designation was made at a meeting of the Council of the City and County of Swansea on 2 October 2025... The Scheme will be effective from 14 February 2026 and, unless revoked beforehand, will cease to have effect on 14 February 2031... Failure to apply for a licence is an offence under Section 72(1) of The Housing Act 2004 for which a person may be fined up to £20,000. An application may also be made to the Residential Property Tribunal to make a Rent Repayment Order requiring the repayment of up to 12 months' rent collected during the time the property was unlicensed.' CORROBORATION: the HMO Licensing Policy 2025 para 6.8 states 'Council, by way of this policy, revokes the designation made in 2020 in respect of Castle, Uplands and St Thomas wards and the subsequent addendum to include Waterfront in 2022, that scheme will cease to have effect on 14 February 2026', and confirms the new scheme 'specifically applies to all HMOs which do not come within the remit of mandatory licensing within the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas wards including HMOs defined under Section 257, Housing Act 2004 i.e. poorly converted blocks of self-contained flats.' Para 1.3 records that additional licensing has run in Castle and Uplands 'since the introduction of the legislation in 2006', with St Thomas added in 2020 and Waterfront in 2021/2022. Para 1.5: 'Additional HMO licensing schemes have a maximum five years duration.' The live service page states 'Additional Licensing applies in the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas wards of Swansea. All HMOs, irrespective of size, have to be licensed in these wards... Student accommodation which is owned and managed by a university is exempt from licensing.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED DECISIVELY, table extracted from the live fees page (last modified 1 April 2026), single discounted payment: 3 occupiers £1,096; 4 £1,176; 5 £1,256; 6 £1,336; 7 £1,416; 8 £1,496; 9 £1,576; 10 £1,656; rising by £80 per occupier to 20 occupiers £2,456. Early renewal runs £1,024 to £2,384. THE LADDER STARTS AT THREE OCCUPIERS, NOT FIVE. A mandatory-only authority's ladder starts at five, so this is conclusive cost recovery for sub-mandatory HMOs and therefore a genuine s.56 scheme. The widely-quoted £2,456 figure is confirmed as the 20-occupier single-payment fee. WARD NAMES VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT REGISTER, THE HIGHEST-RISK ITEM, AND IT PASSES. Swansea's electoral arrangements were reviewed and new wards took effect at the May 2022 elections, which is when Waterfront ward was created. The designation was made on 2 October 2025 and took effect on 14 February 2026, BOTH AFTER that review, so the names are current, not stale. Swansea's live ward list was independently pulled from its democracy site and all four (Castle, Uplands, Waterfront, St Thomas) appear verbatim in the current 31-ward register. NO stale ward names flagged. Coverage is 'wards' because the designation is expressed in whole electoral wards, not streets. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING, EVIDENCED IN BOTH LANGUAGES: zero URLs containing 'selectiv' across 6,744 English sitemap URLs; zero 'trwyddedu dewisol' across 6,890 Welsh URLs, where the only 'dewisol' hits are elective home education and discretionary housing payments; zero occurrences of 'selective' in the full HMO Licensing Policy 2025; and zero across ten further housing and landlord pages. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES. (2) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION: the working brief warned Swansea has one. IT DOES NOT. Zero hits for 'article 4' across the HMO and planning pages. In Wales the C4 use class came into force in February 2016 WITHOUT permitted development rights for C3 to C4, so planning permission is always required and no Article 4 is needed. Swansea's planning control is instead LDP Policy H9 plus HMO and purpose-built student accommodation SPG. The policy itself says at para 1.11 that licensing 'cannot address HMO density issues, which are a Planning matter'. (3) '(ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS) (WALES) REGULATIONS 2007', a s.257 MANAGEMENT instrument. (4) 'FEES FOR ADDITIONAL OCCUPANTS', per-occupier laddering. (5) STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL at policy para 6.1. (6) The s.254 definition at para 5.2. (7) Borough-wide MANDATORY licensing, which is not a designation. LIMITATIONS: swansea.gov.uk returns HTTP 403 to plain requests; this is a BOT BLOCK, NOT EVIDENCE, and adding a browser User-Agent plus Accept, Accept-Language and Referer returned HTTP 200 on every page. The council's own site search is JavaScript-driven and UNUSABLE, the positive control returning a response byte-identical in size to the nonsense negative control, so no nil result from it is relied on. THE PREDECESSOR: the 2020 scheme ceased on 14 February 2026, the same day the new one took effect, so cover was continuous; it is not recorded as a separate object because it is immediately superseded and its precise start date is not published.

notes: Torfaen has no selective or additional licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: three or more storeys and five or more occupiers. A licence costs £708 for five years. Rent Smart Wales registration is a separate national requirement for all Welsh landlords.
research: NEGATIVE, SOURCED, AND THE MAIN PAGE IS A TEXTBOOK STATUTORY-POWERS TRAP. THE TRAP FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: a raw-HTML grep of the HMO page returns SIX hits for 'selectiv' and TWO for 'additional licen'. Every single one is a generic recital of the statutory framework, not a designation. The page says: 'Do all HMOs have to be licensed? No. Under the Housing Act 2004 there are three types of licensing: Mandatory (required by law)... Additional licensing of HMOs - A discretionary power that councils MAY decide to apply to a particular type of HMO... Selective licensing of other residential accommodation - Properties that are not subject to HMO licensing COULD be covered under a selective licensing scheme. This is where the council MAY declare that certain areas... are appropriate for selective licensing.' Note the modal verbs: 'may decide to apply', 'could be covered', 'may declare'. There is NO designation, NO named area, NO commencement or expiry date and NO fee attached to either discretionary type. The hit count is inflated because the page body is duplicated in an embedded JSON content payload as well as the rendered HTML, exactly the collapsed-JSON pattern that causes false positives, so the six hits are really the same two sentences counted three times. This is the single most likely source of a wrong answer at Torfaen. THE POSITIVE EVIDENCE OF MANDATORY-ONLY: (1) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the applying-for-a-licence page states a SINGLE FLAT FEE, 'The fee is £708.00 for a 5 year licence.' There is no ladder, no small-HMO or sub-mandatory band, no per-property fee and no separate application route. That page returns ZERO raw hits for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen'. (2) REGISTER TEST: the public register ('Register updated 5 August 2024') contains exactly ONE licensed property: 'Licence No 151780, Issue Date 31/7/2024, Expiry Date 31/07/2029, Station House, 1 Station Street, Abersychan, Pontypool, NP4 8ph, Max Occupiers 5, Storeys 3.' Five occupiers and three storeys is precisely the mandatory threshold. Under an additional licensing scheme the register would necessarily contain sub-mandatory HMOs; it contains none. (3) SITEMAP SWEEP: the full sitemap (3,522 URLs covering both the /en/ and /cy/ trees) grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol', 'amlfedd' and 'trwydd' returns ZERO hits for every one of those terms in both languages. The only HMO pages on the entire site are the four English pages and their four Welsh mirrors. WELSH THRESHOLD: Torfaen states the mandatory test in the Welsh three-storey form, consistent with WSI 2006/1712 (W.174). OTHER TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES, the reason a Torfaen landlord can correctly be told they need 'a licence' while no local designation exists. (2) The s.254 DEFINITION: 'A House in Multiple Occupation HMO (sometimes called a house share) is a property rented out by at least 3 people who are not from 1 household and who share basic amenities' defines an HMO, NOT a licensing threshold; the 'at least 3 people' figure must not be read as a trigger. (3) The s.257 CONVERTED-FLATS TEST. (4) The 'converting a property to an HMO' planning page. LIMITATIONS: the council's own site search was not relied on; the negative rests on the complete 3,522-URL bilingual sitemap sweep, raw-HTML greps of all HMO pages, the single flat fee and the composition of the public register.

notes: UNVERIFIED: Shared Regulatory Services still states an additional licence is needed for HMOs in the Castleland Renewal Area of Barry, but the Vale's own register and fee list show mandatory licences only. Anyone with an HMO in central Barry should confirm with the council.
research: THIS RECORD IS DELIBERATELY MARKED UNVERIFIED BECAUSE TWO CURRENT COUNCIL-CONTROLLED SOURCES DIRECTLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER on the one question that matters: whether a landlord with a sub-mandatory HMO in central Barry needs a licence today. Getting this wrong in the permissive direction risks an unlimited fine and a rent repayment order, so no confident answer has been forced, and no scheme object is recorded in either direction. WHAT IS SOLID. (a) NO SELECTIVE LICENSING, stated expressly by the council's own regulatory service in both languages, confirmed by raw-HTML grep: the SRS HMO page states 'There are currently no areas of selective licensing.' The Welsh version states 'Ar hyn o bryd, nid oes ardaloedd lle ceir trwyddedu dewisol.' The SRS Business Plan 2026-27 contains zero occurrences of 'selective'. This negative is firm. (b) The Vale delegates HMO licensing to SHARED REGULATORY SERVICES, its statutory joint regulatory body with Cardiff and Bridgend, which is why no HMO page exists on valeofglamorgan.gov.uk itself. A sweep of all 11,591 URLs in the council's own sitemap returns zero hits for 'hmo', 'multiple-occup', 'selectiv', 'dewisol' or 'ychwanegol' outside three old Rent Smart Wales news items. THE CONFLICT, VERIFIED AT RAW-HTML LEVEL. Inside a collapsed accordion on the generic SRS HMO page, visible only on grepping the raw HTML and not the rendered text, the council states: 'If you own or manage a HMO of any type or size in the Cathays or Plasnewydd area of Cardiff which is not subject to mandatory licensing, you will need to apply for an Additional HMO Licence. Similarly, if you own or manage a HMO which isn't subject to mandatory licensing in the Castleland Renewal Area in Vale of Glamorgan, you will need to apply for an Additional Licence.' The Welsh page repeats it. That is a live instruction to landlords, in the present tense, on a council-controlled site. The scheme was genuine historically: the council consulted on a 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Additional Licensing Scheme' for the Castleland Renewal Area with the consultation running until 14 March 2012, and its own HMO Licensing page in January 2016 listed 'Additional Licensing - As in the Castleland Ward' alongside an 'HMO Licensing Enforcement Plan 2012-2017'. FOUR CURRENT PRIMARY SOURCES POINT THE OTHER WAY. (1) REGISTER TEST: the live public register (dated in-sheet 05/01/2026) has a single worksheet literally named 'Public Sheet - Mandatory' holding ten properties, every one 3-4 storeys with 5-9 occupiers. There is no 'Additional' sheet and not one sub-mandatory licence, including at Holton Road, Vere Street and Harvey Street addresses that sit inside the Castleland area. (2) FEE TEST: the Vale-specific SRS page returns ZERO raw-HTML occurrences of 'castleland', 'additional' and 'selectiv', and lists only 'The HMO licensing scheme is to be self-funding and the following fees will apply: Mandatory HMO Licence: £792; Mandatory HMO Licence (Renewal): £657.' No additional-licence fee and no additional application route. By contrast the sibling Cardiff page on the SAME site sets out its schemes, dates, public notices and a graduated additional-licensing fee ladder, proving the site does distinguish scheme types, so the absence on the Vale page is meaningful. (3) SRS Joint Committee 'Fees and Charges', 17 December 2025, lists for the Vale only the two mandatory fees. (4) SRS Business Plan 2026-27 and Annual Report 2025-26 mention additional licensing ONLY as 'Additional HMO Licensing at Cathays and Plasnewydd' and 'Redeclare the Plasnewydd Additional Licensing Scheme in Cardiff'; 'Castleland' appears ZERO times in either. Underpinning this, the council's own archived page for the renewal area says 'The Area was declared in April 2010... The Renewal Area has a twelve-year lifetime', so the underlying renewal designation lapsed around April 2022, and a s.56 designation cannot in any event exceed five years. WHY THIS IS UNVERIFIED RATHER THAN A NEGATIVE: the weight of current evidence (register composition, fee schedules, committee reports, service plans) says the scheme is not operating, and the SRS page is demonstrably stale elsewhere, since it still presents Cardiff's Plasnewydd scheme as running from 1 January 2021 for five years when that ended on 31 December 2025 and the business plan schedules its redeclaration. But a council page telling landlords they need a licence is not something to overrule silently in a product carrying this risk. The public note therefore leads with the conflict and directs the user to confirm with the council. DATES NOT ESTABLISHED: no designation or revocation dates could be found from any primary source. Vale committee minutes are online only from 2019, no 2012 cabinet report is archived, and the 'Additional Licensing' sub-page of the old council site was never captured by the Wayback Machine. WARDS: the Castleland Renewal Area is STREET-DEFINED, and the Vale had major ward boundary changes at the May 2022 elections, so the 2016 page's phrase 'Castleland Ward' is both imprecise and probably stale. NO WARD LIST HAS BEEN SYNTHESISED. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) CARDIFF'S CATHAYS AND PLASNEWYDD SCHEMES, the single biggest attribution risk here because they are described on the very same shared SRS website the Vale uses; they belong to CARDIFF Council. (2) RENT SMART WALES. (3) STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL: 'Where an area of Additional Licensing is designated, the Council can decide on which type of HMO is covered by the scheme' describes the power, not its exercise. LIMITATIONS: the Vale's own site search FAILED its control test, requiring a POSTed viewstate, with every GET including the control query returning 'No results found', so no nil result from it is evidential. Substantial evidence here sits on srs.wales rather than a .gov.uk domain; srs.wales is the Vale's own delegated statutory regulatory service, linked from the council's apply-online page, and its fee and business-plan reports are published on valeofglamorgan.gov.uk, so it was judged authoritative, but this is a departure from a strict .gov.uk-only rule and is flagged. RECOMMENDATION: this record should be resolved by a direct written enquiry to Shared Regulatory Services rather than by further desk research, because the published record is internally inconsistent.

schemes.areaDescription: The whole of Wrexham County Borough. Covers all HMOs except those exempt under the Housing Act 2004.

notes: Wrexham runs an additional HMO licensing scheme across the whole county borough, so all HMOs need a council licence, not just larger ones. The scheme is due to end on 31 December 2026. A five year licence costs £898. There is no selective licensing.
research: ACTIVE s.56 ADDITIONAL LICENSING, COUNTY-BOROUGH-WIDE, BUT EXPIRING IMMINENTLY. THE PUBLIC NOTICE states: 'PUBLIC NOTICE IN RESPECT OF THE INTRODUCTION OF AN ADDITIONAL LICENSING SCHEME FOR HOUSES IN MULTIPLE OCCUPATION IN THE COUNTY BOROUGH OF WREXHAM. This designation is published in accordance with Sections 56 to 60 of the Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of the Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006... The designation applies to the whole area of the County Borough of Wrexham... The designation was made at the Council's Executive Board Meeting on 21st September 2021... The designation will be effective from 1st January 2022 and unless revoked beforehand will cease to have effect on 31 December 2026. The designation applies to all Houses in Multiple Occupation within the County Borough except those exempted by the relevant sections of the Housing Act 2004.' THE PDF WAS PARTIALLY VERIFIED DIRECTLY: it downloads at HTTP 200 and its embedded document title confirms both the instrument type and the county-borough-wide scope. Its body text is drawn in CID-encoded embedded fonts, so the date lines could not be re-extracted from the PDF itself; they were corroborated from the live HTML page instead and they agree. CORROBORATION 1, the live service page: 'As the local housing authority we operate mandatory and additional HMO licensing schemes' and 'At the Executive Board meeting on September 21, 2021 a new five year scheme Additional Licensing Scheme was approved, to begin on January 1, 2022.' A five-year scheme beginning 1 January 2022 ends 31 December 2026, matching the notice. CORROBORATION 2, Executive Board 21 September 2021 item 41, report COPR/50/21: 'That another 5 year additional HMO licensing scheme covering the whole of the county borough be approved to commence on the 1 January 2022.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'New licence (Mandatory Licence or Additional Licence) - 5 years £898 (£493.90 at application, £404.10 before issue). New licence - 1 year £561. Renewal Mandatory Licence - 5 years £898.' The application route is expressly shared between the two regimes, which only makes sense where an additional scheme is live. NOTE the RENEWAL line names ONLY the mandatory licence, consistent with the additional designation running out on 31 December 2026. Wrexham states the mandatory threshold in the Welsh three-storey form. SCHEME HISTORY: a 2011-2016 scheme expiring 31 October 2016; a re-designation report to Executive Board on 12 July 2016; consultation approved 9 March 2021; scrutiny 16 June 2021; designation 21 September 2021. The September 2021 minutes note 'the gap between the current scheme ending and the new scheme starting', because a designation cannot commence until three months after approval. Wrexham has run additional licensing near-continuously since 2011. **EXPIRY WARNING, ACTION REQUIRED: the designation ends 31 DECEMBER 2026, under five months from this record, and NO SUCCESSOR SCHEME WAS FOUND.** Every Executive Board agenda and minutes page from January 2025 to October 2026 was read, and a date-filtered committee document search for 'additional licensing' across that period returns no HMO licensing item; the only 2026 HMO mention is an unrelated Leader's statement objecting to a proposed HMO at Oak Alyn Hall, Gwersyllt. Agendas for the 15 September and 13 October 2026 Executive Board meetings are not yet published, and on the 2021 timetable a 2027 successor would appear there. THIS RECORD MUST BE RE-CHECKED AFTER THOSE MEETINGS AND AGAIN IN EARLY JANUARY 2027, or the product will tell Wrexham landlords a licence is required when the designation has lapsed. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING: the site search returned one irrelevant hit; the full 2,070-URL sitemap across both wrexham.gov.uk and wrecsam.gov.uk, grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol' and 'ychwanegol', contains no selective licensing page; committee hits for 'selective licensing' are OR-matches on 'licensing'. WARDS: the designation is EXPRESSLY whole-county-borough, so coverage is borough-wide and wards is NULL. This sidesteps the May 2022 Welsh ward boundary review entirely, since the designation predates it by four months but names no wards. The Grosvenor Road, Rhosddu and university-area HMO concentration is real as a PLANNING concern but the licensing designation is not limited to it. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES. (2) 'THE LICENSING AND MANAGEMENT OF HMO (ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS) (WALES) REGULATIONS 2007', cited for s.257 converted blocks of flats, a MANAGEMENT instrument. (3) PLANNING CONTROL via UDP local planning guidance notes. (4) 'ADDITIONAL LEARNING NEEDS' and 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol', which dominate the bilingual sitemap on that token. (5) yourvoicewrexham.net, which resolves to a PARKED COMMERCIAL DOMAIN and was not used as a source. SEARCH CONTROLS: the Wrexham solr search PASSED both controls ('multiple occupation' returned 16 results; the nonsense control returned 'Sorry no results were found'), and the committee search passed its negative control, so these nil results are genuine evidence. LIMITATION: the designation instrument itself is only inspectable as a hard copy by appointment at Lambpit Street; the published public notice is the authoritative online text and states the area, dates and scope explicitly.
